ranked_candidates.leak: no module has been proven to stand up STANDALONE and EMBEDDED with the same identities
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH, and structurally so. It is one of three remaining unproven matrix categories and the only one that tests COMPOSITION of modules rather than a single game. Every claim the campaign makes about `mount()` merging rather than ordering is untested with two modules.
ranked_candidates.closeable: PROBABLY, without moving code: Sanic and Mary-O exist in-tree and `PlatformerApp::mount` already takes any `GameModule`. The unknown is whether their content survives being mounted beside another module, which is exactly what the row is for.

ranked_candidates.leak: the ratchet's last entry is rollback, deferred by ADR 0031
ranked_candidates.cost: It is the ONLY thing between the campaign and §4.1.
ranked_candidates.closeable: Yes, trivially and WRONGLY. Curating `ambition::rollback` would take the ratchet to zero tonight.
ranked_candidates.owned: NO — ADR 0031's Deferred section reserves rollback-as-public-knob for its own slice with its own acceptance tests, calling it 'a far larger promise than a clock'.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: NOT owned -> not a slice. ⚠ This is the candidate most likely to be taken by a future reader looking at '1 away from zero'. The contract entry says why not, at the entry.
ranked_candidates.action: blocked on the deferred rollback slice, not on effort

ranked_candidates.leak: 39 of 39 facade dependencies are unconditional; a movement-only game links 19 crates it never asked for
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH but still UNFELT — no consumer has been unable to do something because of it.
ranked_candidates.closeable: Untested. The experiment that would settle it (make the edges optional, re-measure) is contained in one manifest.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: Closeable + Owned -> strong slice-E candidate, and the one that decides whether §4's decomposition trigger ever fires. Deliberately after D, because D adds a SECOND sentinel to measure the footprint against and a footprint measured on one consumer is the same mistake as an API proven against one consumer.

ranked_candidates.leak: the blind run still opens engine files
ranked_candidates.closeable: Partly, and it is not a slice on its own — each run names ONE next thing and the fix is usually small (run 2's was a missing prelude re-export, closed same day).
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: rides alongside every slice. Re-run at the end of each; the run names its own next fix.

slice_d.name: one module, standalone and embedded
slice_d.one_leak: nothing proves a module composes WITH another module — `mount()` is claimed to be a merge with conflict detection rather than an ordering, and that claim has never had two modules put to it.
why_this_and_not_the_footprint: The footprint experiment is cheaper and more dramatic, and it should still wait. §2e is measured PER SENTINEL CONSUMER, and there are two — both of which are single-module games written by me. Measuring optional-dependency reduction against that population would answer 'can a game I designed avoid linking menus', not 'can a game'.

Slice D adds the first consumer I did not design for the SDK: an in-tree demo that predates it. That is the closest thing available to an independent consumer, and §4's carve decision should be taken against it rather than before it.

It is also the last matrix row that is plausibly reachable without new engine subsystems. Smash needs rollback (deferred) and `ambition-itself` is the full integration, so D is where the matrix can still move.
why_it_is_the_real_test_of_ADR_0032: ADR 0032: 'module inclusion is a MERGE, not an ordering. `include(SanicModule)` over a draft is a merge with transactional conflict detection... Over `&mut App` it is did Sanic's plugin run before Mary-O's.'

Every module mounted so far has been alone. `ModuleDraft::claim` already refuses a second experience/route declaration and names both claimants — written in slice A, never exercised by two real modules.

And the identity half is the sharper claim: ADR 0032's deletion criteria require that 'Sanic standalone and Sanic embedded produce the same content and rollback-schema identities'. Nothing has ever compared them.
not_in_this_slice: module-qualified namespaces and pack identity — B's deferred content design. D should find out whether they are NEEDED by trying to embed without them; a namespace scheme designed before the collision is a guess.
the facade optionality experiment (slice E, deliberately after D so it has a consumer I did not design)
rollback as a public knob, and therefore Smash
exit_criteria_sketch: one in-tree module (Sanic or Mary-O) mounts through `PlatformerApp` STANDALONE and boots;
the same module mounts ALONGSIDE the minimal game and both boot;
content and schema identities are compared across the two compositions and the comparison is a TEST, not a printout;
a genuine conflict (two modules claiming one experience id) is refused, naming both claimants — the `claim` path finally exercised by two real modules;
the module gets its own allowlist ratchet with a measured baseline, like every consumer before it;
